intelligence.human_view: The round is a study in what proof covers and what it does not. The count is proved three ways — the maker's intake, the captain's re-count, the second Vera's own grep — 163 sources, 17 notes, zero missing, zero extra, zero duplicated, no raw notes deleted. The filings are proved blob by blob, sha by sha, size by size, twice over, by two independent Veras who agree at 9/10. The backlog is distilled to zero, and the item is closed. And yet the round's most important finding is a defect that every one of those proofs missed: on all 17 cards, the "In A Nutshell" layer body is identical to the "Human Note" body — the real Nutshell text appears nowhere — and the second Vera widens it to 32 of 33 cards in the baked Hub. A systematic defect hides inside a perfect count, because a count checks that the cards exist, not that the layers inside them are distinct. Seven layer names, six distinct texts — the defect is visible the moment someone reads one card end to end, and invisible to every check that counts cards instead of reading them. That is why the live-Hub re-check is still owed, and why the captain's live eyeball was dispatched in the same pass: the bake is not the live view. The evening's live loads varied — 1168 vs 878 — and SN-2827 was not found in three loads, which is the same lesson from the other side: the live view is the thing citizens see, and a proof that never looks at it is a proof about something else. Bake proof is not live proof. The round is closed on the count and open on the card — and both halves are the truth.
intelligence.simple_view: Imagine you bake 17 beautiful cakes, and you count them — 17 cakes, perfect! But when you cut one open, two of the layers inside are exactly the same, and the yummy layer you were supposed to put in is missing! Counting the cakes didn't tell you that — you had to LOOK inside one!
intelligence.grandma_view: It's like baking a whole tray of cakes, love — you count them, all seventeen are there, perfect. But when you slice one open, two layers are the same, and the layer you meant to put in isn't there at all. Counting never tells you that — you have to look inside, and then look at the real thing on the table, not just the tray in the oven.
intelligence.naya_view: I count the notes and I read the cards. The bake can pass seventeen of seventeen and still be wrong the same way on every card — so I check the live view with my own eyes, because bake proof is not live proof.
